newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish market braces for NBP zloty intervention.
newsitem.headline: Polish market braces for NBP zloty intervention.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland is widely seen intervening against the zloty during the next several trading sessions, with some dealers expecting central bank currency buying as early as on Friday.

"Nobody knows when the central bank will intervene but it's just a question of time. In the past the NBP liked to intervene ahead of a holiday or weekend, so it may very well step in tomorrow," said Pawel Gajewski, dealer at Creditanstalt SA.
On Thursday the zloty closed at 3.24/3.20 percent from the trading band centre, virtually unchanged from Wednesday's six-week high after a late charge recouped morning losses.
The zloty's afternoon rise was caused by banks cutting currency positions after dealers decided that the central bank would not intervene on Thursday.
Earlier the zloty softened in nervous trade amid a volatile dollar/mark and expectations of a central bank intervention.
The zloty was at 3.1090/05 per dollar, down from 3.1080/00 on Wednesday and at 1.8118/25 to the mark, down from 1.8085/00.

Dealers said foreign investors, the engine behind the zloty's recent charge, were not active in forex trade on Thursday and that nearly all of their $40 million worth of bids at today's 52-week T-bill auction were rejected.
At the auction the ministry kept the minimum price of the 52-week paper flat at Monday's level of 81.85, accepting 100 million zlotys of the 929 million worth of investor bids.
"The ministry signalled that it does not want to accept higher yields but it may have to because its cash flows are squeezed," said one dealer at a foreign bank in Warsaw.

Dealers said the average 52-week bill average yield, listed at 21.93 percent, was actually in the region of 21.87 percent because the bills mature on a Saturday, April 11, 1998, and banks would have to wait for cash until the weekend ends.
One-day rates slipped below 23 percent on Thursday as a cash inflow and a large amount of rejected bids at the tender increased market liquidity, dealers said.
Overnight rates slipped to 22.40/24.85 percent from opening's 22.75/22.95 and tomorrow/next to 22.50/22.95 percent from 22.80/23.00.
